newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly up, palladium mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly up, palladium mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended mostly higher on Friday, backed by strong bullion prices and the yen's dip against the dollar, traders said.

Palladium futures settled mixed after shedding some of their early gains as a view that Russia may resume its exports of platinum group metals to Japan in the near future prompted market players to take profits.
Gold futures ranged from 22 yen to 31 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark February was up 24 yen at 1,393 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $353.00/30 per ounce at 0750 GMT, against $353.10/60 in New York on Thursday.
In gold futures, private investors, who were taking profits in the morning session, switched to fresh buying later as the dollar leapt against the yen by late Tokyo, the traders said.
"Sentiment towards gold has improved. Yen-based gold futures are likely to rise further as the yen may dip further," one trader said.
Spot gold was relatively steady during Asian hours.
Traders said gold may probe the upside if a slump in the U.S. stock market continues.
In white metals, profit-taking capped early gains while buying by overseas investors supported the market.

One official at a major bullion house said he has not yet heard from the Russian platinum group export agency when the Japan-Russia export contract talks will be held, but he said it was possible that Russia will resume spot selling by the end of March. Palladium futures ranged from seven yen per gram lower to 10 yen up, with benchmark February down seven at 578 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen to 30 yen per gram up. Benchmark February was up eight yen at 1,479 yen.
Benchmark February silver was up 4.7 yen at 209.6 yen.
